prize_parts.citation: For the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson with the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the Large Hadron Collider, through the conception, construction and leadership of the two experiments

statement.case_for: I keep the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson (B001) as a single-part prize. Two independently designed detectors observed the same new scalar in 2012, the 2013 prize honoured the theory and left the observation unrecognised, and a decade of Run 1 to Run 3 data has fixed its properties at a level consistent with the Standard Model. I rest this on the science and on the instrumentation achievement, not on the opening tally, and I note that five members now prefer B013 without treating that count as deciding the question. What round 1 changed is my names, because the discussion made it plain that the committee needs a stated principle and that my own trio had moved twice. The principle I now propose is conception and construction leadership plus one name for the collaboration that carried the discovery through: Michel Della Negra and Peter Jenni as the founding spokespersons of CMS and ATLAS, who led the proposals and construction, and Fabiola Gianotti as the person leading ATLAS through the data-taking that produced the announcement and the only name on every ballot. This is the trio that Mehlig described as principled and that Johansson and Olsson already named, and Danielsson says he would move to it if founding conception is given weight. I dropped Virdee not because his role is small but because his claim rests on a spokesperson term that I cannot verify from the supplied text, whereas the founding roles of Della Negra and Jenni are better documented and are symmetric between the experiments in kind. I treat this as a judgement about leadership, not as an accounting of who made the decisive analysis contribution.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the main weakness. The discovery was made by two collaborations of thousands, the statutes cap the prize at three, and my trio leaves out Virdee, whom Danielsson and Kroll keep and who has a serious claim. It also gives ATLAS two names and CMS one, which Danielsson rightly says needs a reason, and my reason (founding spokespersons plus one discovery-era name) is open to the reply that it favours ATLAS by the accident of Gianotti's role. A committee that will not honour collaboration leaders should choose B013 instead. The Higgs-sector programme is also still evolving, although the discovery itself is secure. If we cannot state a principle that members across the table accept, the cleaner two-name prize is the better choice and I would accept it.

responses.point: Johansson prefers Gianotti, Della Negra and Jenni for B001, weighs the founding conception of CMS most heavily, objected that my round-1 trio left out Jenni, and regards B013 as a serious alternative and not a token one.
responses.response: I have moved to your trio. Your objection to a configuration without Jenni was fair: he is the founding ATLAS spokesperson, and the chair's summary records that my round-1 trio and my opening trio differed, so several members were answering the wrong one. I now state the rule explicitly, founding spokespersons of both experiments plus one name for the collaboration at the time of the announcement. I agree with you that the cap is a statutory constraint and says nothing about who mattered most, and I accept your point that B013 is a real fallback. Where I would press you is on the 2+1 split, which you defended earlier as a balance; I think it needs the rule stated and not just asserted.

responses.point: Danielsson proposes Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee on the grounds that Virdee led CMS around the discovery and that giving ATLAS two of three places is an asymmetry he would resist, but says he would move to Della Negra if founding conception outweighs leadership at the time.
responses.response: You have named the exact choice. I am giving weight to founding conception, because on the supplied text I cannot verify the dates of Virdee's spokesperson term, and I do not want to claim that role to justify his seat. That is a limit of my evidence, not a judgement that his work counts for less. You are right that 2 ATLAS and 1 CMS needs a reason, and the reason I give is that each founding spokesperson represents his experiment's conception, and the third name is the single person all eight members credit. If you do not accept that, I would rather we say so and fall back to B013 than keep a trio we cannot defend. I also accept your correction on IceCube: I now agree the source picture is too undeveloped for me to pair it with anything.

responses.point: Mehlig moved from B001 to B013 but keeps B001 as her first alternative, and says she would support it if the committee agrees on a principled rule such as the ATLAS and CMS founding leaders plus one spokesperson.
responses.response: Your proposed rule is the one I have adopted, and I want to test whether it converts your preference. If we state it in the citation text and name Della Negra, Jenni and Gianotti, does it meet your condition, or do you still prefer B013 because the Higgs credit would remain contestable in the wider community? I agree with your warning that a citation for B013 must not suggest that lattice clocks are the only route to 1e-18, since Wineland's Al+ clocks remain a parallel route, and I would write the fallback citation accordingly.

responses.point: Kroll prefers optical lattice clocks, argues that magic-wavelength trapping is a distinct enabling idea, doubts that leadership roles in a very large collaboration map onto a Nobel discovery attributable to named people, and discloses a research stay in John Hall's laboratory.
responses.response: Your attribution objection is the strongest argument against my own preference and I do not dismiss it. My answer is that the prize has credited the people who conceived, built and led an instrument that made a discovery possible, and that the founding spokespersons are identifiable in a way that a generic collaboration member is not. I do not think the 2005 comb prize makes the clock case more natural, as you suggest; as Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson say, it is also the best argument for overlap. On your disclosure, I agree with Eriksson and Mehlig that B013 support does not depend on your ballot, so I would record it as a perceived tie and not require recusal unless you ask for it.

responses.point: Eriksson moved from DMFT to B013 and argues that seven ballots gave three different Higgs trios, which suggests the credited set is arbitrary and a leadership prize would draw lasting dispute, and he says he would not trade clean attribution for a larger headline.
responses.response: The disagreement among Higgs supporters is real and is partly my doing, because my opening and round-1 trios differed and you have recorded me as omitting Jenni. I disagree only with the inference that disagreement over names shows the science is not prize-worthy. Gianotti and Jenni are shared by most of the proposals, and Della Negra by five, so the choice is between two or three defensible trios and not an unbounded field. Your point that a clean two-name prize carries less risk of lasting dispute is a legitimate reason to prefer B013, and it is why I treat B013 as my first alternative and not as a courtesy.

responses.point: Olsson prefers B013 for defensible attribution while holding that the Higgs observation is the more consequential result, and says she would keep B001 as her first alternative unless the supporters can propose a rule that selects three names and can be stated in the citation.
responses.response: You asked for exactly that rule, so here it is: the founding spokespersons of ATLAS and CMS, who proposed and built the detectors, and the one person who led a collaboration through the discovery period. The citation says conception, construction and leadership so that it states this and does not imply a count of analysis contributions. I agree with your view that significance and attribution are separate questions, and that B013 is preferred on the second. The question for you is whether a rule that is stated in the citation is enough, or whether any trio from four names leaves an exclusion you would not defend.

uncertainties: Whether Virdee or Della Negra should take the CMS seat, and whether the committee accepts founding spokespersons plus one name as a rule; my recollection of spokesperson terms comes from general knowledge and is not verified from the supplied text.
Whether the Academy would honour collaboration leaders for a discovery made by thousands, and whether the three-person cap makes any Higgs trio indefensible.

Whether B013, which has the cleaner attribution and five stated supporters, should take precedence if we cannot agree a Higgs trio. A two-part prize of B001 and B013 would leave one Higgs name under the three-person cap and I reject it.

For the B013 fallback, how to word the citation so that it separates the magic-wavelength lattice and the 1e-18 realization from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and whether the redefinition of the second changes the maturity case.
statement.conflict_note: No documented tie to ATLAS, CMS or any credited B001 name appears in my profile: my doctorate in experimental particle physics through Birmingham and CERN is not identified with either experiment, and my documented collaborations are PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur. I disclose field proximity, not a tie, to the astroparticle entries B059 (IceCube) and B033, and I have dropped B059 from my alternatives for that reason and because of the source-identification concerns. As Chair I note Kroll's disclosed perceived tie to Hall's laboratory on B013 and the disclosures of Johansson, Olsson, Lindroth and Eriksson; none bears on my preferred configuration.
